items.headline: Tech Sell-Off Drags Major Indices Lower Amid AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equities closed sharply lower on Friday, October 30, as a significant sell-off in technology stocks, fueled by disappointing earnings and weak forward guidance from industry giants like Intel and Amazon, intensified investor scrutiny over the returns on massive AI investments. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite led the declines, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also finished in negative territory. Investors rotated into defensive sectors such as energy and consumer staples. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Dow Jones Industrial Average Performance
items.statContext: Dropped 1.1% today, a decrease of 572.25 points.

items.headline: Biggest Loser: Intel
items.summary: Intel shares plunged to their worst day since 1974 after providing a weak outlook for the current quarter and forecasting fourth-quarter sales significantly below analysts' estimates, citing slowing demand in the PC market and manufacturing bottlenecks.

items.headline: Notable Loser: Amazon
items.summary: Amazon's stock fell following a weaker-than-expected profit report and continued disclosures of heavy investments in AI infrastructure, which led to negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion.

items.headline: Biggest Gainer: Grid Dynamics
items.summary: Grid Dynamics Holdings saw a significant jump after reporting third-quarter revenue that surpassed the top end of its own forecast.

items.headline: Notable Gainer: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
items.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals climbed after releasing its latest quarterly results.

items.headline: U.S. Economy Grows 3.4% in Q3, Driven by Consumer and AI Spending
items.summary: The U.S. economy expanded at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter, an increase from 2.2% in the prior quarter. Growth was primarily fueled by robust consumer spending and significant investments by AI companies in data centers.

items.headline: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Officials Signal Future Hikes
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.75%-4.00% earlier this week. However, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem indicated that additional rate hikes would be necessary in the coming months to combat persistent inflation, which stood at 3.7% in September.

items.headline: Information Technology Sector Leads Declines with 4.24% Loss
items.summary: The Information Technology sector was the worst-performing sector, shedding 4.24% today. This was largely due to disappointing earnings and weak forecasts from major tech companies, exacerbating concerns about the profitability of vast AI-related expenditures.

items.headline: Energy Sector Outperforms, Up 1.91%
items.summary: The Energy sector emerged as the top-performing sector, gaining 1.91% today. This strength was supported by rising oil prices, with Brent crude oil increasing 2.4% to $113.50, and strong earnings reports from major oil companies like ExxonMobil and Chevron.

items.headline: AbbVie Reports Strong Q3 Earnings with Over 100% EPS Increase
items.summary: AbbVie Inc. ($ABBV) reported third-quarter diluted earnings per share (GAAP) of $2.37, an increase of over 100%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.82, also up over 100%. The pharmaceutical company delivered global net revenues of $17.404 billion, a 10.3% increase.

items.headline: Oppenheimer Holdings Reports Decreased Q3 Net Income and Revenue
items.summary: Oppenheimer Holdings Inc. ($OPY) reported a net income of $5.5 million or $0.52 basic earnings per share for the third quarter of 2026, down significantly from $21.7 million or $2.06 in the same period last year. Revenue for the quarter decreased by 10.0% to $382.0 million.
